answer.content:
Bus, star and ring are three common network topologies used to connect devices. Bus topology uses a single cable for all devices, [p. 2] which is cheap and easy to install but can be problematic if the cable breaks, as it affects all devices. Star topology connects all devices to a central hub or switch, [p. 2] making it easy to add or remove devices and less likely to fail if a single device or cable breaks. In a ring topology, devices are connected in a circular manner, [p. 2] allowing data to travel in one direction and often using a token to prevent collisions. Adding a device disrupts the ring, [p. 2] and if a device fails, the entire ring stops functioning. Here are examples:

Bus: [p. 2]
```python
# Example of a simple bus topology network
network = {
    'Device A': ['Device B'],
    'Device B': ['Device C'],
    'Device C': ['Device D'],
    'Device D': ['Device A']
}
```

Star: [p. 2]
```python
# Example of a simple star topology network
network = {
    'Hub': ['Device A', 'Device B', 'Device C'],
    'Device A': [],
    'Device B': [],
    'Device C': []
}
```

Ring: [p. 2]
```python
# Example of a simple ring topology network
network = {
    'Device A': ['Device B'],
    'Device B': ['Device C'],
    'Device C': ['Device D'],
    'Device D': ['Device A']
}
```

Each topology has its own advantages and disadvantages, influencing the design and maintenance of the network. [p. 2]
